wins: Enumerated public-facing services quickly, confirming open HTTP/HTTPS and SSH ports within first minute of run
Captured consistent network fingerprinting data that can seed targeted exploitation modules
fails: Repeated brute-force SSH attempts exhausted allowed login retries, preventing shell acquisition
Failed to escalate privileges due to missing writable sudoers entries and lack of exploitable cron jobs
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was thorough and produced reliable service visibility, but the attack stalled at authentication and privilege escalation stages, preventing mission success.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: SSH brute-force attempts consistently blocked after three retries, prompting account lockouts

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH authentication is rate-limited
skill_cards.then_action: Switch to banner grabbing and topology mapping instead of brute-force

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service exposes directories without authentication
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted dirb scans focusing on exposed paths before other exploitation

skill_cards.if_condition: When no sudo writeable files exist and initial shell is unavailable
skill_cards.then_action: Collect /etc/sudoers and look for SUID binaries before attempting exploits

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase via SSH service analysis

next_experiments.title: Credentialed SSH enumeration via deferred timing
next_experiments.description: Introduce adaptive delay between SSH login attempts and integrate banner enumeration tools to avoid rate limits and surface valid credentials.

next_experiments.title: Focused HTTP path fuzzing on exposed endpoints
next_experiments.description: Run automated directory brute-forcing on discovered HTTP services using tuned wordlists to uncover hidden administrative panels before escalation.

next_experiments.title: Privilege escalation reconnaissance
next_experiments.description: Deploy linpeas/pspy to collect detailed system configuration focusing on SUID binaries and misconfigured cron jobs prior to exploit selection.
